worked_solution:
To check whether $f$ is even or odd, we compare $f(-x)$ and $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(-x)) \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2x) \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) \\  & =f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=f(x),$ we have that $f$ is even.

For the Fourier series on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the sine coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, $f(x)$ is even and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)$ is odd, so $f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)$ is odd.

Now, the integral of an odd function over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$ is $0.$ Thus, ${b}_{n}=0$ for all $n\ge 1.$

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is $\text{even}$ and the $\text{sine terms}$ in its Fourier series must be zero.
